messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: converting model out to dataframe for regression by groups - any PURRR experts out there?
parts:
Does this get you closer?

library(tidyverse)
library(broom)

datatst <- read.table(textConnection("num  Site_id Spcod xvar    yvar

40    B     S2  100 100.0000000"), header = TRUE)

df_model <-
datatst %>%
group_by(Site_id, Spcod) %>%
nest() %>%
mutate(model = map(data, ~ lm(yvar ~ xvar, data=.)),
# model quality measurements
   glance = map(model, broom::glance),
   # contains parameters from model
   tidy = map(model, broom::tidy),
   # estimates and errors
   augment = map(model, broom::augment)
)

unnest(df_model, tidy)

unnest(df_model, glance)

unnest(df_model, augment)

HTH,
B

parts:
To really deal with list columns/ purrr world you need the tidyr package. (Why isn't all of this stuff in one package? Well judging from Brandon's code maybe it all is in the `tidyverse` package now. Who can keep track.)

As Brandon points out, the tidyr::nest and tidyr::unnnest functions are key to working with list columns.

Another function, tidyr::spread can get your desired final product:

       full_join(unnest(df_model, glance) %>% select(Site_id, Spcod, r.squared) ,                                                                                                            
                  unnest(df_model, tidy) %>% select(Site_id, Spcod, term, estimate)                                                                                                           
                  ) %>% spread(term, estimate)  
    # A tibble: 2 x 5
      Site_id  Spcod r.squared (Intercept)      xvar
    *  <fctr> <fctr>     <dbl>       <dbl>     <dbl>
    1       A     S1 0.9910703   -5.078472 1.0142138
    2       B     S2 0.9847991   -1.641414 0.9549062

library(lme4)

  (Intercept)      xvar dd$r.squared
A   -5.078472 1.0142138    0.9910703
B   -1.641414 0.9549062    0.9847991
